data.title: Puf6 ushers correct rRNA compaction during ribosome assembly
data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled to mass spectrometry was used to study the complex between the nucleolar factor, Puf6, and the yeast 60S ribosome. Disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS) was used as the cross-linking reagent.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Chemical cross-linking was performed following previously described procedures (Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014). The sample was digested using endoproteinase Lys-C followed by trypsin and the digest was fractionated by size-exclusion chromatography. Two SEC fractions were analyzed in duplicate by data-dependent LC-MS/MS on a Thermo Orbitrap Elite system. File numbers 156/157 and 158/159, respectively, are replicate injections of the same fraction. Additional details are provided in the accompanying publication.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest/xProphet (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.4, against the sequences of target proteins (Puf6 and ribosomal proteins) and identified contaminants.  Additional search settings were as follows: Enzyme = trypsin, maximum number of missed cleavages = 2, MS mass tolerances -5 to +5 ppm, MS/MS mass tolerance = 0.2 Da for “common”-type fragment ions and 0.3 Da for “xlink”-type fragment ions. The original scoring scheme of xQuest (Rinner et al., Nat. Methods, 2008) was used. xProphet was used to adjust the false discovery rate to <5% at the nonredundant peptide pair level.
keywords: Chemical cross-linking; dss; structural proteomics; ribosome; ribosomal assembly
